meaning:
ἐκ-τρέπω
[in LXX for הָפַךְ, Amo.5:8 * ;]
to turn out of the course, turn aside, with accusative Pass., with middle sense, intrans., to turn aside: Heb.12:13 (R, txt., for be put out of joint, R, mg., see Thayer, see word Westc., in l); figuratively, before εἰς, 1Ti.1:6; ἐπί, 2Ti.4:4; ὀπίσω, 1Ti.5:15; with accusative, to shun, avoid: 1Ti.6:20.†
(AS)

renderings.kjv: be turned out of the way

elsewhere.note: from which things some, having missed the mark, have turned away to vain talking,
and will turn away their ears from the truth, and turn away to fables.
and make straight paths for your feet, so what is lame may not be dislocated, but rather be healed.
